citation: Herrera et al. 2000 Measuring the effects of pollinators and herbivores: evidence for non-additivity in a perennial herb
closest_contribution: Direct pollinator-present/excluded x herbivore-present/excluded factorial on maternal fecundity; establishes interaction-dependent plant fitness.
remaining_gap_to_sch: No multi-level randomized shared trait axis and no reconstruction of state-specific trait optima.

citation: Ågren et al. 2013 Mutualists and antagonists drive among-population variation in selection and evolution of floral display in a perennial herb
closest_contribution: Factorial supplemental pollination x grazer exclusion identifies opposing agents on a genetically based floral-display dimorphism; long-term grazer exclusion shifts morph frequency.
remaining_gap_to_sch: Trait is a standing binary morph rather than randomized multi-level z; no continuous state-specific fitness optima or experimental optimum-shift surface.

citation: Sletvold, Moritz & Ågren 2015 Additive effects of pollinators and herbivores result in both conflicting and reinforcing selection on floral traits
closest_contribution: Factorial manipulation of pollination and herbivory intensity identifies agent-mediated selection on phenology, display and spur length.
remaining_gap_to_sch: Trait values are not randomized; selection gradients under manipulated interaction states do not reconstruct bounded state-specific nonlinear trait optima.

citation: Sun, Armbruster & Huang 2016 Geographic consistency and variation in conflicting selection generated by pollinators and seed predators
closest_contribution: Geographic observational evidence that exsertion/lip traits track both pollen receipt and seed predation, with antagonist-weight mosaic and pollination-success/risk coupling.
remaining_gap_to_sch: No randomized z, no selective P/G intervention and no causal optimum shift.

citation: Fitch & Vandermeer 2021 Can conflicting selection from pollinators and nectar-robbing antagonists drive adaptive pollen limitation?
closest_contribution: Defines antagonist-induced adaptive pollen limitation; manipulates floral display in experimental arrays and combines survey/experimental evidence to estimate an optimum flower number.
remaining_gap_to_sch: No independently crossed pollination-weight and antagonist-access states on the same randomized trait surface; no z x P x G state-optimum shift test.

citation: Pérez-Barrales et al. 2013 Pollinators and seed predators generate conflicting selection on Dalechampia blossoms
closest_contribution: Integrated observational fitness surface links larger display to more pollen and more seed-predator eggs, with compromise-like stabilizing net selection.
remaining_gap_to_sch: No randomized display axis or independently manipulated P/G states; state-specific causal optima remain unidentified.

citation: SCH prospective P. rex z x P x G causal surface
closest_contribution: Prospectively crosses >=5 realized z levels with supplemental-vs-natural pollination dependence and independently excluded-vs-exposed seed predators on one mature-seed fitness scale.
remaining_gap_to_sch: Prospective design only; novelty is not empirical until the registered experiment is executed successfully.
